question: Which experiences create satisfaction, and what should we protect?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Satisfaction in this index comes almost entirely from the 1,000 recorded phone conversations, and what creates it is an agent who explains something clearly and finishes the job on the call.** In that conversation corpus 47.6% of contacts end mildly positive and 13.7% strongly positive. The 4,425 written complaints contain almost none of it: 2 positive contacts in total. That is a property of the sources, not a change in customer mood, so read the rest of this answer as "what a good phone contact looks like", not as "customers are getting happier".

The largest single source of positive sentiment is clear communication, present in 366 contacts, ahead of helpful staff at 241 and a fair outcome at 101. The pattern under those labels is consistent: the customer arrives not knowing something (which account to pick, what a fee is, how to set up a payment) and leaves knowing it. The three biggest positive themes are all of this kind - advice on account types and features (138 contacts), step-by-step setup guidance (99) and clarification of fees and limits (67).

The second ingredient is completion. In the conversation corpus 608 of 1,000 contacts end resolved; in the complaints corpus 31 do. Positive contacts are the ones where the agent did the thing during the call - submitted the application, set up the transfer, reserved the box, waived the fee - rather than routing it onward. Where agents had discretion to improvise, satisfaction was highest: helpful staff carries a mean sentiment of 1.29, the strongest of any positive driver.

What to protect, concretely: the agent authority to complete account setup, transfers and fee waivers in one contact; the explain-then-act habit that makes clear communication the top driver; and the fallback path from self-service, since several of the most positive contacts begin with a customer who could not finish the task online. Protecting these matters most where the complaint corpus is worst - the same explain-and-finish behaviours are exactly what unexplained closures and denied disputes lack.

caveats: The index holds two corpora: 4,425 real written complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations (September 2023 only). Unfiltered numbers mix them.
Essentially all positive sentiment comes from the conversation corpus. A complaint channel selects for dissatisfaction, so the contrast measures the sources, not a change in how customers feel.
The conversations are synthetic and cover a single month, so the satisfaction drivers below are a picture of good handling, not a measured satisfaction rate for the bank.
Sentiment, resolution status and driver categories are model-extracted per contact, not survey scores; treat the ranking as indicative rather than exact.
followups: If we captured sentiment on real phone contacts rather than synthetic ones, would clear communication still outrank a fair outcome as the top driver?
How many of the complaint themes - unexplained closures, denied disputes - would have ended differently with the same explain-and-finish handling seen in the positive conversations?

confidence.badge: moderate · 1,000 calls · 1 month · concentrated in one month
